title: Strengthen PinEntryWidget's error-styling test to assert the border color, not just decoration non-null
why: The test 'should have error styling when error message is present' (pin_entry_widget_test.dart:206-225) only asserts `firstField.decoration != null`, which is unconditionally true — the widget always sets a decoration whether or not hasError is true (its own comment admits 'which we can't easily test'). But it can: pin_entry_widget.dart:266-268 picks the border colour from `theme.colorScheme.error` vs `.outline` based on hasError, and that colour is directly readable off `decoration.enabledBorder` without pixel-level rendering. If that branch were deleted or inverted, this test would keep passing — a real regression in the parent-PIN wrong-attempt affordance would ship with green CI.
recommendation: Rewrite the assertion to read `(firstField.decoration!.enabledBorder as OutlineInputBorder).borderSide.color` and compare it against `theme.colorScheme.error` in the error case and `.outline` in a matching non-error case.
acceptance_criteria: Test fails red when pin_entry_widget.dart's hasError ternary at line 266-268 is temporarily reverted to always return theme.colorScheme.outline, proving it actually exercises the branch.
